title: BECE Mathematics Statistics & Probability - Mathematics - Data Presentation
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Which of the following charts uses sectors of a circle to represent data?
questions.explain: A pie chart represents data using sectors of a circle where the angle of each sector is proportional to the frequency of the data.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: In a pie chart, the total angle at the center of the circle is:
questions.explain: A full circle represents the total data, which corresponds to an angle of $360^\circ$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: A student spends 8 hours sleeping in a day. What is the sector angle for sleep in a pie chart representing his daily activities?
questions.explain: Sector angle $= \frac{\text{Value}}{\text{Total}} \times 360^\circ$. A day has 24 hours. Angle $= \frac{8}{24} \times 360 = \frac{1}{3} \times 360 = 120^\circ$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: In a frequency table, what symbol is used to represent a count of 5 items using tally marks?
options: An oblique line crossing four vertical lines
questions.explain: A standard tally for 5 is four vertical strokes crossed by a diagonal stroke.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: If 40 students took a test and 10 of them passed with an A, calculate the sector angle for grade A in a pie chart.

questions.q: Which diagram uses pictures or symbols to represent data?
questions.explain: A pictogram uses pictures or icons to represent specific quantities of data.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: In a bar chart, the height of the bar usually represents the:
questions.explain: In a standard bar chart, the height (or length) of the bar corresponds directly to the frequency of the category.

questions.q: The main difference between a bar chart and a histogram is:
options: Bar charts have gaps between bars, histograms do not
Bar charts are for continuous data
questions.explain: Bar charts generally represent discrete categories with gaps, whereas histograms represent continuous data intervals with no gaps between bars.
